items.review_rationale: Read the N-1 criterion and distinguished integral closure inside the fraction field K from N-2 closure inside all finite extensions L/K. Here the normalization inside K must be finite as an R-module.

references.phrase: integral closure of R inside K

references.disposition: The ambient ring is specifically the field of fractions, not an arbitrary extension and not algebraic closure.

items.review_rationale: Read the graded-ring and forgotten-grading Noetherian condition, plus both chain and finite-generation descriptions. Homogeneous ideal chains and arbitrary ideal finite generation are not interchangeable without the stated equivalence.

references.disposition: This is a graded chain property; the definition also explicitly requires finite generation of each ungraded ideal.

items.review_rationale: Read the inverse limit as a submodule of an infinite direct product with compatibility φ_n(m_n)=m_{n−1} at each step. The definition is not a direct limit or a product without compatibility.

references.context: Module theory: infinite product of R-modules, coordinatewise addition and R-action

references.disposition: Compatibility is required for every n≥2 and defines the inverse-limit submodule.

items.review_rationale: Inspected the arrows M_n→M_{n−1} for all n≥2, the positive-integer index and composites to earlier terms; this is the contravariant/inverse direction and not a module direct system.

references.phrase: inverse system over an ordered index

references.disposition: The transition maps compose according to the inverse index direction and satisfy coherence; they need not be isomorphisms.

items.review_rationale: Read the finite-type algebra presentation k[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_c) and the dimension equality dim(S)=n−c. This is the stated global criterion, not an assertion that any finite presentation is a complete intersection.

references.context: Commutative algebra: polynomial k-algebra in finitely many indeterminates
Commutative algebra: quotient of polynomial ring by finitely generated ideal of relations

references.disposition: This is an equality about the presentation and Krull dimension; no unspecified regular-sequence criterion is being substituted.

items.review_rationale: Read local complete-intersection algebra via a covering of Spec(S) by standard principal open affines D(g_i), with S_{g_i} globally complete-intersection over k. No equality of local complete intersection and global complete intersection is assumed.

references.context: Algebraic geometry: basic Zariski open subset defined by nonvanishing of a ring element

references.disposition: Every point of Spec(S) belongs to at least one specified open, and each corresponding localization must be globally complete-intersection.

items.review_rationale: Read all three closed immersion criteria: homeomorphism onto a closed subset, surjectivity O_X→i_*O_Z and locally generated kernel. The topological closed embedding alone is insufficient.

references.phrase: morphism of locally ringed spaces i:Z→X

references.context: Topology: homeomorphism from Z to subspace topology on a closed subset of X

references.phrase: pushforward sheaf i_*O_Z and surjective sheaf map
references.context: Sheaf theory: direct image of sheaf along i and epimorphism or locally surjective map of sheaves of rings
Algebraic geometry: kernel sheaf of ideals locally generated by sections

references.disposition: This is a substantive local condition additional to closed topological image and map surjectivity.

items.review_rationale: Read the closed locally ringed subspace determined by a locally section-generated ideal sheaf I⊆O_X, with support Z of the quotient and quotient structure sheaf whose direct image equals O_X/I. Preserve both sheaf and topology conditions.

references.phrase: locally section-generated sheaf of ideals I⊆O_X
references.context: Sheaf theory and algebraic geometry: ideal subsheaf with local section generators

references.phrase: support Z of quotient sheaf O_X/I
references.context: Sheaf theory: support of a sheaf or module sheaf, with stalk-based nonvanishing

references.phrase: quotient sheaf O_X/I and direct image under inclusion
references.context: Sheaf theory: quotient of a sheaf of rings by ideal sheaf and direct image i_* of a sheaf

references.disposition: This is an equality of sheaves of rings on X, not just their stalks as abstract rings or a set-level quotient.
